text: We could have said, first-time offenders, no increase, but it may cut against the very policy that we are seeking to put in.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In a way – and this is where Members of Parliament come in – we should see whether we can help them when they come and see us through the community to help the lower-income drivers, to help them pay the fines.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That, the Traffic Police would take a sympathetic approach.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I think the framework should be kept intact.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Chairman, our operating landscape will continue to change.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Society will change and progress, and there will be new uncertainties and crises that will emerge.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have outlined some of the approaches we take to try and deal with that and to be future-ready, as it were.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: My fellow Ministers and officeholders will answer the other questions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, I will focus on the Home Team's increasing use of science and technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MHA established the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) in December 2019.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Patrick Tay asked how the Home Team will tap the expertise within HTX to mitigate emerging threats and manpower constraints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will talk about three Centres of Expertise today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the past few months, HTX has developed customised solutions to augment our Police and Civil Defence operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These solutions allow us to optimise our scarce manpower, and increase operational capacity and agility.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, HTX worked with the Police to develop the Multi-Purpose All Terrain Autonomous Robot 3.0 (MATAR 3.0).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MATAR 3.0 is a fully autonomous patrol robot.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Compared with its previous models, MATAR 3.0 has added features, such as a tethered Unmanned Aerial Vehicle for aerial surveillance and enhanced cameras for long-range surveillance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: You can imagine how useful such a device is in terms of sensemaking as well as redeploying resources appropriately.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another application of robotics is to save lives in disaster rescue efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Urban search and rescue missions are extremely dangerous, particularly at sites where no terrain information is available, such as collapsed buildings or post-disaster sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, HTX is studying the use of robots designed to mimic animals in their functions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One such robot is ROVER-X, which can move and manoeuvre like a dog.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By customising ROVER-X with navigational capabilities, thermal cameras and sensors, we can deploy it in hazardous terrains that are unsafe for humans and reduce the time required to find and rescue victims.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Later this year, HTX will be testing additional use cases for ROVER-X, such as monitoring hazardous materials, inspecting chemical plants, and supporting the security of key installations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The use of automation and unmanned systems can also alleviate resource-intensive operations, like the ongoing fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the support of HTX, the Police are progressively deploying closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras equipped with video analytics and motion sensors at some Government Quarantine Facilities, to enhance the security of the premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our second Centre of Expertise targets chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive threats (CBRNE).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CBRNE threats can pose significant risks to public safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the last 10 years, MHA has set up a network of CBRNE detection laboratories and a Bio-Surveillance Programme along our borders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These are our first line of defence against CBRNE threats.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The labs enable frontline units to detect and intercept dangerous materials at our checkpoints, and support investigations and intelligence gathering by the Home Team departments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are plans to expand the detection labs to more checkpoints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bio-Surveillance Programme, which was set up to detect bioterrorism threats at our checkpoints, is also able to detect other agents, such as influenza and health-concerning pathogens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Using a state-of-the-art system, which integrates laboratory functions on a small chip, our scientists can quickly adapt the system to detect new biological agents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This capability was demonstrated in the ongoing COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MHA has deployed this kit as part of our Bio-Surveillance Programme at our land, sea and air checkpoints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The third Centre of Expertise focuses on digital forensics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: DIGEST will relieve the workload of Police Investigation Officers, so that they can focus on other aspects of investigative work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will also be extended to other Home Team departments, such as CNB.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The fast-growing ecosystem for the Internet Of Things means that everyday devices, such as smart watches, home appliances and vehicles, can contain important evidence to support investigations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: HTX is developing capabilities to harness data from Internet Of Things devices to support investigations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The above examples illustrate how HTX works closely with the Home Team to develop solutions to protect our safety and security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Moving forward, HTX will play a master-planning role to identify and develop cross-cutting capabilities across the Home Team.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will facilitate greater cooperation and synergy, so that we adopt a unified One Home Team approach in keeping Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Home Team departments are also constantly refining their operations to tap on technology to deliver better services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, ICA has been digitalising its services to achieve its customer-service vision of "No Fuss, No Visit, No Waiting", and this will be for Singapore residents and travellers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: ICA has already embarked on several initiatives in line with this service vision.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, Singaporeans can look forward to a more hassle-free and efficient immigration clearance experience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I know, of course, during this period, no one is thinking of travelling very much.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, the idea of breezing through customs and border control is not so exciting.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the time will come when our airport will be very busy and so will the other checkpoints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is something that we can deploy to effectively manage the voluminous flow of passengers in and out of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The results of the trial were successful and ICA has since extended the trial to Changi Airport Terminal 4.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I agree with Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Jessica Tan that it is important that the Home Team prepare and equip our officers to adapt to technological transformations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the wide spectrum of capabilities the Home Team requires, HTX will recruit talent across practically all disciplines of science and engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will need scientists trained in life and physical sciences for the development of crime forensics and CBRNE detection capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will need electrical, mechanical and software engineers who can work in blended teams to realise operational systems, such as advanced video sensors and robotics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last but not least, we will need computer scientists and engineers to tackle the challenges posed by data and digital technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They will be deployed in various roles, from cybersecurity to developing algorithms, to augment the Home Team's frontline response.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have already seen strong interest in HTX as a career.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They were a good mix of fresh graduates and mid-career professionals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This year, we will ramp up recruitment even more.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As we build deep science and technology capabilities within HTX, we will concurrently build up a cadre of uniformed officers who are grounded in operational experience and proficient in technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To nurture such officers, we are progressively introducing an "Ops-Tech Career Track" for Home Affairs Uniformed Services officers across the Home Team departments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There will be structured pathways to enhance these officers’ operational experience and exposure to technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These officers can also embark on further studies to develop technical knowledge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Together, the HTX and Ops-Tech officers will work together with the larger Home Team workforce to innovate and deliver solutions to support the Home Team’s mission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, I will speak on two areas: combating drug abuse and strengthening the rehabilitation and reintegration of offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: New psychoactive substances (NPS) are a rising threat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: NPS mimics the psychoactive effects of traditional drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are seeing a global movement towards more liberal attitudes on drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: More countries are legalising drug abuse or are considering to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They gloss over documented harms of cannabis, like mental disorders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Pro-legalisation camps also conveniently ignore the social costs – lives lost, families destroyed, increased crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singapore is not immune to a worsening global drug situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: First, the attitudes of young Singaporeans towards drugs are changing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: An MHA survey found that youths in Singapore have more liberal views on drugs, particularly, cannabis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A decade ago, NPS was hardly known in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Now, NPS is the third most commonly abused drug.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: More than ever, we need strict laws to stay ahead of drug trends, robust enforcement and effective preventive drug education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On NPS, we have been proactively listing NPS to the Misuse of Drugs Act (MDA) since 2010.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But as Mr Christopher de Souza pointed out, the difficulty is that rogue chemists are able to swiftly produce new NPS variants by changing their chemical structures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This poses a challenge for drug enforcement agencies the world over.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MHA is reviewing our laws to stay ahead of drug trends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Effective preventive drug education must achieve two important aims.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: First, our people must know the facts about drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And second, the effort must garner community support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Strict laws and robust enforcement require the people's backing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Mohamed Irshad asked how we help our youths stand firm against drug abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about our strategies against cannabis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In schools, we teach the facts about drugs through story-telling and activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A cartoon activity book for preschoolers will be ready in April, an Anti-drug Ambassador Activity (AAA) booklet has been used by over 48,000 primary school students in 2019 and 60 secondary schools have been offered an after-school anti-drug engagement programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Information on the harms of drugs must be easily understood and put in layman terms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For instance, as suggested by Mr Christopher de Souza, we state in our press releases how many abusers have their drug addictions fed from drugs found on a trafficker.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To counter growing misinformation about cannabis, we are making facts about cannabis accessible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have a one-stop repository for cannabis-related information on CNB's website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Infographics on the harms of cannabis and the social costs of legalising cannabis are on social media platforms, and an anti-cannabis information booklet for educators will be ready this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, to win community support, a one-way exchange of information will not be enough.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: At the heart of what we do is to speak with our people frankly, give them the facts, hear them out, and involve them to co-create and deliver.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The National Council Against Drug Abuse (NCADA) will launch "HIGH", an interactive film by Royston Tan, in March.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Viewers get to make choices and learn the consequences of their choices in this film.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: At our preview screenings, we invited youths to no-holds barred conversations on drugs, revealing its ugly, gritty realities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We co-created projects with youths from all institutes of higher learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: One-hundred and sixty youths are our Anti-Drug Abuse Advocates and they have organised four roadshows and campaigns raising awareness amongst their peers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Republic Polytechnic and Nanyang Polytechnic students created two anti-drug games to teach about the harms of drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Institute of Technical Education (ITE) students have produced anti-drug videos and Temasek Polytechnic students had a social media campaign on how drugs affect our loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Mr Mohamed Irshad asked about community anti-drug engagement efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have been working on with various groups – youths, LGBTQ+, ethnic communities, parent groups and others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Last September, Indian youths and 13 Indian community groups organised the Bothaiporulai Ethirtu Nirpom (BEN) campaign.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: BEN is a short form, a Tamil phrase – "We Stand United Against Drugs".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Indian celebrity, Anand K, helped as an anti-drug ambassador.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We gave out envelopes and snack packets with anti-drug messages at the Deepavali bazaar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We worked with various LGBTQ groups on anti-drug campaigns, discussion forums, research and outreach activities in support of a drug-free lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now speak in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   Our efforts to free the community from the evil grip of drugs have become more important.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: More countries now have a more open attitude towards drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Worryingly, they are unable to manage the drug problem within their own societies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I remember attending an international drug rehabilitation conference in Argentina last October.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The number of drug offenders has jumped in many countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They feel defeated and some had to liberalise their laws against drugs because it has become unmanageable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We multiply the Government's effort, we do not give up and we do not shirk away from difficult tasks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our society is exposed to influences from abroad and in the cyber world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The myth is that cannabis is not harmful This is totally wrong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Surveys by MHA have shown that Singapore youths have a more open attitude towards drugs, especially cannabis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We must not stand still or get complacent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The strategies to combat the drug menace will be strengthened.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The three strategies are tighter laws, stronger enforcement and a more effective drug prevention education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am pleased to announce that, this year, MHA will focus more efforts on two things.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is the Government's pledge: we will continue to work with Malay organisations, families and our young people to protect our community and our families, and prevent us from being enslaved by drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For those in need, we will help them to recover and continue their journey towards excellence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The M³ movement led by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), the Council for the Development of the Singapore Malay/Muslim Community (MENDAKI) and the People's Association Malay Activity Executive Committees Council (MESRA) has focused its attention towards offenders and their families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MUIS has launched the Family and Inmates Through-care Assistance Haven (FITRAH) programme in November 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MENDAKI organised the Family Excellence Circle programme to assist caregivers, offenders and couples.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MESRA will customise several courses from the SHIOK series to meet the needs of the families of ex-offenders, especially for the young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Malay organisations, such as the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP), the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS), the Muslim Missionary Society Singapore (JAMIYAH), the Singapore Muslim Women's Association (PPIS), Club Heal and the Harun Ghani Education Fund, are also ready to assist.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The "Dadah Itu Haram" campaign continues to receive solid support from motorcycle enthusiasts, fishing hobbyists, asatizahs as well as dikir barat and theatre activists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Forty-two mosques as well as 200 shops and organisations also have come forward to help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Currently, over 75 barber shops support the campaign by becoming informal anti-drug advisors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These barbers are learning more about the harmful nature of cannabis and share with their clients about the harms in order to counter the myths surrounding cannabis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will look at the effectiveness of these efforts through surveys that are taking place currently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This year, we will focus on family and youth programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, I will now speak about the rehabilitation and reintegration of offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked how the amendments to MDA in 2019 has affected inmates' risks of re-offending.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The full suite of MDA changes took effect last August, so it is still early to make any conclusions on their impact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked how we can reduce re-offending.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Prisons will strengthen support for offenders in three ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Prisons has started the Family Interventions and Reintegration Support Team (FIRST) trial, and family case managers work with community partners to support inmates' families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Over 100 inmates have benefited from this trial and the results are encouraging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Prisons will be enhancing collaborations with social service agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, a network of positive peers to support ex-offenders stay crime-free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Prisons will expand its Throughcare Volunteer Framework to encourage more volunteers and support inmates pre- and post-release.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Inmates will be empowered to take charge of their rehabilitation through the Prisons' Digitisation of Inmate Rehabilitation and Corrections Tool (DIRECT).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Inmates use shared tablets to learn and keep in touch with their loved ones via electronic letters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCORE prepares offenders for employment through employer engagement, skills training and employment assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: More than 5,600 employers from various industries offer jobs to ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Almost 6,000 offenders went for an average of four training courses each last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Over 2,600 offenders received employment assistance, with 96% securing jobs before prison release.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCORE will further support inmates to get industry-relevant skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCORE will partner Singapore Precision Engineering and Technology Association (SPETA) and Mediacorp to set up precision engineering and media skills training academies this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, colleagues, the choices we make today affect tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will keep Singapore safe and secure together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I have 12 cuts to cover.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I seek your indulgence, if I eat slightly into clarification time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Chairman, I will focus on MHA's efforts to tackle tech-enabled crimes and also our partnerships with the community for crisis preparedness.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will also address the questions raised by Members.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Technology has changed the way in which criminals operate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Social media platforms offer criminals a new means of targeting victims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Foreign syndicates use the Internet and spoofing technology to obscure their identity and conduct illegal activities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our enforcement capabilities must keep pace with technological developments.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Last year, we saw a significant rise in Police reports of scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Dr Tan Wu Meng asked what more can be done.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police have been enhancing their capabilities to disrupt such activities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, the Anti-Scam Centre was set up in 2019 to mitigate the losses of victims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The committee will coordinate approaches and efforts across the Government and pool resources.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But even as the Government steps up efforts to combat scams, we cannot do it alone.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Businesses have a role to play, too, especially those, such as e-commerce platforms and banks, which can also be exploited by scammers, causing monetary losses to customers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will work closely with such businesses to put in place upstream measures to limit the ability of criminals to do harm.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That said, the best defence against scams continues to be a discerning public.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Criminals are looking to exploit people's feelings for loved ones or other personal motivations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We urge the public to be sceptical of incredulous promises, to utilise escrow accounts provided by the platforms for transactions where possible, and to check with the authorities when approached by dubious people purporting to be Government officials.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police will continue to work with the National Crime Prevention Council to engage the community and spread this message.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Chairman, I would now like to make a few remarks in Mandarin.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: (In Mandarin):   Scammers are constantly devising new ways to ensnare their victims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With the increase in online transactions, online scams have also increased.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Government will be setting up an inter-Ministry committee to discuss how to tackle scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Businesses also have to take responsibility and establish secure platforms for transactions to effectively protect consumer rights.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For the public, the best defence against scams is to stay vigilant and discerning.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We urge the public to do transactions only on trustworthy platforms and utilise escrow accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If you have any doubts, please check with the relevant authorities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Let us be vigilant so that the scammers do not stand a chance (In English): Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the actions taken against those who pose as charities to solicit donations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Depending on the facts of the case, the person may also be liable for offences in the Penal Code or the House to House and Street Collections Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked what we will do to tackle the unlicensed moneylending (UML) situation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police will work with stakeholders, such as banks, to take action against suspected UML runners.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The fourth anti-UML campaign was also launched in January 2020.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing suggested that messages from UMLs and sports betting syndicates should be made more easily reportable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to explore ways for such spam messages to be reported more conveniently.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Leon Perera raised a question on regulating gambling, specifically loot boxes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If so, we may block the game from being accessed from Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The game operator may also be liable under the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the Home Team’s efforts to combat human trafficking.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our officers undergo regular training on how to recognise the tell-tale signs and respond sensitively to victims of human trafficking.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our agencies exchange information on human trafficking syndicates with our foreign counterparts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked whether LTVP+ can be granted to all foreign spouses of citizens.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our policy for transnational couples is generally to facilitate the formation of stable families here.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: An LTVP+ may be granted later if the marriage proves stable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the matter of rental housing, the couple can apply for a rental flat if they have a citizen or PR child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For those with other household structures, HDB will consider their request on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Patrick Tay, Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the Home Team's plans to partner the community to deal with threats to our safety and security.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are fortunate that Singapore has not experienced a terror attack in the past few decades, but we must not be complacent.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Terrorism causes loss of lives, injuries and damage to properties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to roll out customised programmes for different domains, such as schools, workplaces, neighbourhoods and community groups.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To enhance the community's first response for cardiac arrest victims, we launched the Save-A-Life initiative in 2015.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked how SCDF will continue to provide efficient and effective Emergency Medical Services (EMS).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Still, one out of 10 calls received are false alarms or non-emergencies.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This ensures that SCDF resources are only used for emergency cases.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: SCDF will continue to raise public awareness on when 995 should be called.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To conclude, the Home Team will develop stronger capabilities to deal with new challenges, but more importantly, we need to work in partnership with the community.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Together, let us build a safer and more secure home.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In these sorts of situations where a person is victimised and has been made to part with money, in fact, there are two legal recourses.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Given the number of scams that Members of the House have seen, life savings being parted, my clarification is, really, of those two options, would the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) and the Police, in appropriate circumstances, prefer the criminal prosecution route under the Penal Code?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: This is much more convenient for the victim who has already lost a lot of money and does not require the victim to go and take out a separate civil suit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It was unfortunate to see the first case of labour trafficking in Singapore, but it is also good to see that there was a prosecution for labour trafficking.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I understand the statistics to be that most of the human trafficking prosecutions are sex trafficking.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: What can we do to prioritise more prosecutions and investigations under labour trafficking?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the first question he had, as I mentioned in my answer, depending on the facts of the case, the person may be liable for offences under the Penal Code, Cheating, section 420, which the Member referred to, and also potentially under the House to House and Street Collections Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will share more details in due course.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, both SPF and MOM work jointly together to make sure that they are enforcing, taking precautions against both sex trafficking as well as labour trafficking.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The officers are actually trained to look out for either both sex trafficking or labour trafficking offences.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Mr Chairman, I have two clarifications for Minister Shanmugam.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: These pertain to the cut that I filed on traffic summonses.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I just want the Minister to confirm that because it has not been my experience when I write in to the authorities that residents have the option of paying those summonses by way of instalments.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I have had that experience with ICA and the Land Transport Authority but not the Traffic Police.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second question I have pertains to the Minister's point about the suggestion I had on potentially halving the fine.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not just halving the fine for the sake of it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In other jurisdictions, they halve a fine for different policy purposes, mainly to make sure people pay their fines.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But there are other policy objectives that can be considered, for example, in the case of beating a red light, which is a very serious offence; I concede that point.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: What you can potentially have is, halving of a fine, but also making sure that that offender goes to the Traffic Police.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If it has to be a programme where he sees what the potential impact can be of these offences, people dying, there also could be some possible policy benefits insofar as greater awareness of road safety, as an example.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I think we do not want a situation where everyone comes and asks for the flexibility.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, there has got to be a rubric or framework.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We are approaching it in the same way, in the sense that we both recognise, and everybody recognises, there are some people who need help, and the question is how best to help them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, one is flexibility that is offered by the Traffic Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The second, which can cover a larger group, would be for the Members of Parliament to help, for them to approach their Members and for them to help through utilising community resources for those who deserve or need the help.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, that I have done it, many Members of Parliament have done it, I am sure the Member would have done it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But also for the Traffic Police, you write in.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the situation is such that the person needs some flexibility, that can be given.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second point on halving the fine, if I understood the point rightly, it is to achieve the policy objective of persuading them or encouraging them not to commit the offence again.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think we are on the same ground here, in that we ought to try and look for ways in which we encourage people not to re-offend.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When they looked at other jurisdictions, a variety of things.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We even considered the possibility of people with different income levels paying different amounts; that is tried in some countries, too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we decided it did not quite work.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have it kept in view (KIV-ed) it to relook.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But for a variety of reasons, it did not seem to work very well, but we will certainly look at the suggestions that Mr Pritam Singh has made.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I thank the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary Mr Amrin Amin for his response to my cut speech on Rehabilitating and Reintegrating Ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I welcome the pilot project that he announced about involving the family in the rehabilitation of ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I wonder in relation to the aftercare scheme for these ex-offenders, particularly those ex-offenders who were involved in gang activities leading to offences being committed, or committing offences as a result of negative peer influence, whether after they have been released, the circle they keep can be monitored, so that they would be prevented from rejoining the gangs or relinking up with friends who caused the offences in the first place.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, there are various programmes and we are happy to invite Mr Murali Pillai to join us and we will see how we can share more about our work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for that reply.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The first is: is there a pathway for LTVP holders to obtain permanent residency if they are in a stable marriage with a Singapore Citizen spouse?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: That is because there is considerable uncertainty without such a pathway, there might even be cases where a Singapore Citizen child might grow up without knowing whether one of their parents has the right to remain in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The second clarification is: would the Senior Parliamentary Secretary be able to elaborate on the housing situation, maybe at the Ministry of National Development's (MND's) COS debate, for such families or, otherwise, put more information out because, again, there are a lot of uncertainties out there for such families about what are their rights for housing and how can they achieve stable housing?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We recognise the importance of keeping Singapore Citizen families, especially those with Singapore Citizen children, intact as far as possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I had mentioned the LTVP+ in my response.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It was introduced in 2012 to provide more support to foreign spouses of Singapore Citizens whose marriages have been stable over time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It also has quite a lot of benefits.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It provides greater certainty of stay, additional benefits, such as inpatient healthcare subsidies that already are at a level that is similar to that of PRs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Whether or not the foreign spouse qualifies yet for PR, I think the fact of the matter is that when you have the LTVP+, you are assured of a significant length of stay in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: He or she can also continue to remain in Singapore and also seek permanent residency when the time comes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If there are other family structures, then HDB will look at it on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If the Member would like further discussion on it, depending on how much time we have at MND's COS debate, I will try to take it up at that juncture as well.
